knowledge:
- key_parameters: geno.file=Path to the input genotype file, which can be either a PLINK bed file or a VCF file ;; print=Integer controlling the verbosity of the output during execution (e.g., print=0 to suppress output)
- alternatives: None mentioned in the documentation
- when_to_use: When you need to classify Helicobacter pylori genomes into reference subpopulations and estimate ancestry proportions using VCF or PLINK genotype data.
- pitfalls: Interactive plotting functions (interactiveReferencePlot, interactivePlot) and the Shiny application require an interactive R session to run.

workflows.name: h_pylori_genome_classification
workflows.intent: Classify Helicobacter pylori genomes from a VCF or PLINK file into reference populations and visualize the classification results.
input: geno.file (VCF file or PLINK bed file containing H. pylori genotypes)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the GrafGen package ;; 2. Run the classification algorithm on the genotype file using grafGen ;; 3. Inspect the classification table and population counts ;; 4. Generate static plots of genetic distance scores ;; 5. Create interactive plots of the reference and user data ;; 6. Launch the interactive Shiny application for filtering and viewing results
workflows.code:
library(GrafGen)
dir <- system.file("extdata", package="GrafGen", mustWork=TRUE)
geno.file <- paste0(dir, .Platform$file.sep, "data.vcf.gz")
ret <- grafGen(geno.file, print=0)
ret$table[seq_len(5), ]
print(ret)
plot(ret)
if (interactive()) interactiveReferencePlot()
tmp <- createApp(ret)
if (interactive()) {
    reference_results <- tmp$reference_results
    user_results      <- tmp$user_results
    user_metadata     <- tmp$user_metadata
    shiny::runApp(tmp$app)
}
